findings.problem: Greek has Μόρκον (Morcus, an Illyrian name), not the Roman Μᾶρκος; ch. 11 of the same book correctly reads Morcus.

units.note: Instruction clause 'first to take whatever hostages from Gentius Pantauchus thought fit' loosely renders ἐκεῖνον πέμπειν (Gentius is to send), but the sense survives; not flagged.

findings.quote: That embassy also succeeded in persuading the Rhodians to join the war.
findings.problem: Greek ἔπεισε δὲ καὶ τοὺς Ῥοδίους συνεμβαίνειν εἰς τὸν πόλεμον has no 'embassy' as subject; the subject is Perseus, continuing from the preceding sentence. The aorist is also odd against the Rhodians' actual course (ch. 10-11, they sue for peace), so the text may be corrupt or conative.
findings.proposed_fix: He also persuaded the Rhodians to join in the war.

units.note: Possible corruption/conative sense (ἔπειθε?); if the editor prefers to preserve ambiguity, add a note rather than assert success.

findings.quote: and then, when he came close to the wall at Demetrias, spoke first with Menecrates and then with Antimachus
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna (***) after τῷ τείχει, before ἐκοινολογεῖτο, and another (* ** ) after Ἀντιμάχῳ before εἴρηται; English reads on as if whole. Also τὸ μὲν πρῶτον ... τὸ δὲ δεύτερον = 'the first time ... the second time'.
findings.proposed_fix: and again, when he came close to the wall at Demetrias, [text lost] he conversed, the first time with Menecrates and the second with Antimachus, [text lost]

findings.quote: And the fact that Herophon twice went as an envoy from Perseus to Eumenes
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna (***) between Ἡροφῶν and ἐπρέσβευσε that the English smooths over.
findings.proposed_fix: And, further, that Herophon [text lost] twice went as envoy from Perseus to Eumenes

units.note: Opening 'I have already stated' rests on εἴρηται, which stands after a gap; the main verb context is lost. Chapter ends mid-sentence in Greek (τίς δ᾽ ... continues in ch. 7); English joins the two halves smoothly, acceptable.
Greek breaks off at τὴν ἐλ[πίδα]; completed in ch. 8; English handles this acceptably.
Numbers (500 and 1500 talents, fourth year) correct. 'later reached' for μετ᾽ ὀλίγον is slightly loose ('shortly after') but not a sense error.

findings.quote: Accordingly, Perseus’ dealings with the Gauls and with Gentius were of a piece with this—
findings.problem: Greek ἀκολούθως δὲ τούτοις Περσεὺς καὶ τὰ πρὸς Γαλάτας καὶ τὰ πρὸς Γένθιον *** breaks off in a lacuna; the predicate is lost. English invents 'were of a piece with this' as if the sentence were complete.
findings.proposed_fix: Accordingly, in keeping with this, Perseus’ affairs with the Gauls and with Gentius [text lost]

units.note: Opening sentence: Greek μὴ καὶ μωροποιεῖσθαι συμβαίνει τὴν φιλαργυρίαν is obscure or corrupt (passive μωροποιεῖσθαι, odd μή); the English 'not only does harm' has no Greek counterpart. No fix proposed, only flagged as ambiguous.

findings.quote: as I have explained in my discussion of public speaking
findings.problem: Greek has the bracketed [ὡς ἐν τῷ περὶ δημηγορίας τέθειται], passive 'as is set down in the (work) on public speaking', an editorial or cross-reference gloss in brackets, not a first-person statement by Polybius.
findings.proposed_fix: [as is set down in the work on public speaking]

findings.quote: When the envoys from Gentius, together with those led by Parmenio and Morcus and accompanied by Metrodorus, arrived at Rhodes
findings.problem: Greek τῶν περὶ τὸν Παρμενίωνα καὶ Μόρκον, τῶν παρὰ τοῦ Γενθίου, καὶ σὺν τούτοις τοῦ Μητροδώρου: Parmenion and Morcus ARE the envoys from Gentius, and Metrodorus came with them. English wrongly implies two separate groups of envoys.
findings.proposed_fix: When Parmenion and Morcus, the envoys from Gentius, and with them Metrodorus, arrived at Rhodes

findings.quote: the number of cavalry that had been lost, and Gentius’ defection crushed them
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna (***) before ἡ τοῦ Γενθίου μετάθεσις; English reads on as if whole.
findings.proposed_fix: the number of cavalry that had been lost, and [text lost] Gentius’ change of side crushed them
